paper_title: What do Patients Wish Their Psychiatrist Had Asked—But Never Asked? A Narrative Review of the Unspoken Agenda in Psychiatric Consultations
paper_abstract: Objective: To synthesise evidence on what patients wish their psychiatrist had asked but did not, why these questions go unasked, what follows from the silence, and which interventions close the gap. Methods: Narrative review, reported against the SANRA scale, of literature identified through PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, the Cochrane Library and Google Scholar to November 2025, integrating conversation-analytic and observational studies, service-user surveys and qualitative research, systematic reviews and meta-analyses, and randomised trials. Results: Evidence converged on eight domains: medication purpose and exit; sexual function; physical health and weight; suicidal thoughts; trauma; work, money and company; identity and stigma; and how information and decisions are handled. The gap is measurable. The patient's preferred approach to receiving information was rated at the lowest possible level in 80 of 80 recorded consultations; 34% of service users reported being offered a choice of medication, whereas 57% of clinicians believed they always or nearly always offered one; sexual dysfunction was detected in 58% of patients on direct questioning but 14% spontaneously; and 70% of patients concealing suicidal ideation feared practical consequences, chiefly hospitalisation. Five mechanisms suppress enquiry: disconfirming question design, divergent agendas, power and prior coercion, stigma, and time pressure that is largely perceived. Structured consultations, question prompt lists, decision aids, specific clinician training, trauma-informed enquiry and routine outcome monitoring have supporting evidence. Conclusion: The unasked question is a systematic, measurable and clinically consequential feature of psychiatric practice, linked to concealed risk, non-adherence, unmet need and disengagement. The deficit is one of implementation, not knowledge. Practice implications: Psychiatrists should replace disconfirming questions with open invitations, ask every patient how they want information and decisions handled, enquire routinely across the eight domains, make the consequences of disclosing suicidal thoughts transparent, and embed structured patient-agenda tools in routine care.

paper_title: Generative AI and Cognitive Processes in Education: A Narrative Review and Conceptual Framework
paper_abstract: Generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) is increasingly being integrated into educational practices, transforming how students access information, develop ideas, and carry out cognitive tasks. While GenAI offers opportunities to foster critical thinking and creativity, its use raises concerns regarding "cognitive offloading"—the delegation of reasoning processes that are fundamental to learning. This study presents a review based on 108 documents from Scopus and Web of Science, which allowed for an examination of the relationships between GenAI, critical thinking, creativity, and cognitive offloading, as well as their pedagogical and institutional implications. The evidence analyzed suggests that GenAI can improve immediate task performance, facilitate idea generation, and support content development. However, these benefits do not necessarily translate into autonomous learning or greater creative originality. Outcomes appear to depend on students' prior knowledge, their AI literacy, task design, metacognitive regulation, and the nature and timing of pedagogical support. Based on this review, an AI-Mediated Cognitive Infrastructure Framework (AMCIF) is proposed, which links GenAI usage patterns with cognitive processes, educational practices, and institutional conditions. This framework distinguishes between forms of assistance that promote cognitive engagement and those that might replace the mental activity necessary for learning, emphasizing the essential role of instructor mediation, source verification, reflective practices, and process-oriented assessment. The AMCIF provides a conceptual foundation for analyzing how to integrate GenAI into educational settings while preserving critical judgment, creativity, and the capacity for independent reasoning. The proposed relationships require rigorous empirical validation.

paper_title: Beyond Animal Models: A Comprehensive Review of In Vitro, In Silico, and Organ-on-Chip Methods for Assessing Pharmacological Safety and Effectiveness
paper_abstract: Background: Traditional animal models in preclinical pharmacology show limited predictive accuracy for human outcomes due to interspecies differences, contributing to high drug attrition rates and ethical concerns. Recent regulatory changes have pushed the development of alternative, human-centered methods.Objective: To comprehensively investigate and evaluate novel non-animal approaches for establishing pharmacological safety and efficacy, such as organ-on-a-chip technologies, in vitro systems, and in silico models.Methods: A narrative evaluation of existing literature was conducted, concentrating on the technological principles, pharmacological applications, predictive performance, and regulatory acceptance of alternative testing strategies.Results: Compared with traditional 2D cultures, advanced in vitro models such as 3D organoids and iPSC-derived cells exhibit greater physiological relevance. Rapid, economical, and high-throughput predictions are made possible by in silico methods such as QSAR, PBPK modeling, and AI-based technologies. With improved translational fidelity, organ-on-a-chip technologies mimic the dynamic microenvironments of human organs. Strong, mechanism-based safety assessment frameworks are produced by integrated testing procedures that combine these methods. But there are still issues with scalability, validation, and standards.Conclusion: With growing regulatory approval for their future application, the incorporation of alternative approaches signifies a paradigm change toward more ethical, human-centered, and predictive drug development.

paper_title: A Structured Review of Distributed Quantum Computing: Infrastructure, Protocols, Applications, Compilation, and Security
paper_abstract: Distributed quantum computing (DQC) connects quantum processing units (QPUs) to execute programs beyond the capacity of a single processor. Understanding its scalability requires examining the interactions between hardware, communication, software, and security. This structured review synthesizes 126 studies, mainly published between 2020 and 2026 with foundational earlier work, retrieved from eight sources and selected using documented inclusion and exclusion criteria. We organize the literature into five pillars: infrastructure, protocols, applications, compilation, and security. A common scoping rule distinguishes work enabling distributed computation from broader quantum communication research. The synthesis identifies interconnect rate and fidelity, classical control latency, remote-operation overhead, and coherence constraints as coupled limits on distributed execution. Infrastructure and protocol research includes experimental demonstrations, whereas application and compiler evaluations remain predominantly simulation-based. Security requires both protected interconnects and confidential, verifiable delegated computation. Comparisons across the pillars reveal tradeoffs between local computation, communication resources, sampling overhead, and trust assumptions. The review highlights unresolved challenges in distributed fault tolerance, transduction, interoperable software, benchmarking, and integrated security. Its central conclusion is that scalable DQC requires coordinated hardware–software–network design and evaluation of complete systems rather than isolated improvements within individual layers.

paper_title: Iron Supplementation in Early Childhood and the Spectrum of Neurocognitive Development: A Systematic Review and Meta-Analysis
paper_abstract: Introduction: Iron deficiency during pregnancy and early childhood may affect myelination, neurotransmission, and neural network maturation, with potential consequences for motor, cognitive, and language development. Objective: To quantitatively synthesize the effects of iron supplementation on motor, cognitive/global, and language development by integrating the original dataset with a complementary search for original studies. Methods: Systematic review with random-effects quantitative synthesis. The expanded review included 11 publications. Continuous outcomes and adjusted estimates were harmonized to log odds ratios (logOR), with positive values indicating better performance with greater iron exposure. Between-study variance was estimated by restricted maximum likelihood (REML). Ten motor, 11 cognitive/global, and 7 language effect estimates were pooled. Results: For motor development, the pooled effect was logOR 0.31 (95% CI 0.14 to 0.48; OR 1.36; p < 0.001; τ² = 0.044; I² = 69.3%). For cognitive/global development, the pooled effect was logOR 0.11 (95% CI -0.10 to 0.33; OR 1.12; p = 0.307; τ² = 0.088; I² = 74.8%). For language, the pooled effect was logOR -0.02 (95% CI -0.26 to 0.21; OR 0.98; p = 0.851; τ² = 0.048; I² = 50.7%). Conclusion: The expanded synthesis yielded a positive pooled estimate for motor development, whereas pooled cognitive/global and language estimates remained close to the null. Effect magnitude and direction varied across populations, timing and dose of supplementation, baseline iron status, and age at assessment.
paper_authors: Maria Adriely Machado de Castro Oliveira

paper_title: What do Patients Remember 24 Hours and One Week After a Psychiatric Consultation, and Does Recall Influence Adherence? A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Objective: To synthesise evidence on what patients retain 24 hours and about one week after a psychiatric consultation, the determinants of that retention, whether recall influences treatment adherence, and which interventions improve recall and adherence.Methods: A narrative review, structured according to SANRA criteria, of systematic reviews, meta-analyses, randomised trials and observational studies, prioritising studies that verified recall against recorded consultation content. Evidence was organised around a causal model running from communication through encoding, retention, comprehension, beliefs and intention to adherence.Results: Across medical settings, 40–80% of consultation information is forgotten almost immediately and about half of what is recalled is inaccurate. At one week, only 49% of decisions and recommendations are freely and accurately recalled (85% with prompting), with a steep educational gradient (38% vs 65%). Direct data at 24 hours, and psychiatry-specific data at either interval, are scarce. Disorder-related deficits in effortful encoding (depression) and free recall (schizophrenia; d = 1.21 vs 0.64 for recognition) compound ordinary forgetting. Communication quality predicts adherence (19% higher risk of non-adherence with poor communicators; 1.62-fold higher odds after training; OR 5.82 for conversational repair in schizophrenia), but knowledge correlates only weakly with adherence and is outweighed by necessity–concern beliefs, insight, depression and alliance. Personalised recordings, written material, explicit structuring and teach-back reliably improve recall but improve adherence inconsistently.Conclusion: Recall is a necessary but insufficient condition for adherence in psychiatry; its link to behaviour is heavily mediated by beliefs and confounded by mood.Practice implications: Psychiatrists should engineer recall deliberately—limit and prioritise content, structure it explicitly, provide personalised written or recorded summaries and verify understanding with teach-back—while simultaneously addressing medication beliefs, mood and the therapeutic alliance.

paper_title: World Models for Digital Agents: An Agent-Centric Survey
paper_abstract: Digital agents operating in software-defined environments, including games, web interfaces, mobile GUIs, tool-use systems, and code repositories, often benefit from anticipating the consequences of actions before execution. World models provide a principled mechanism for such anticipation, but their utility in digital settings is neither automatic nor uniform. Unlike physical environments, digital transitions are interface-mediated and program-governed, and the value of prediction depends less on perceptual realism than on preserving functionally relevant consequences for downstream decisions. This survey presents the first dedicated agent-centric treatment of world models across major digital-agent domains. We introduce a unified design space, W = (X , L, U), organized around three complementary questions: what is modeled, how predictive capability is built, and how world models are used inside the agent loop. Through this lens, we synthesize a rapidly growing literature spanning semantic transition models, visual and latent simulators, tool-state predictors, executable code-based world models, and hybrid predictive systems. We further examine environments, datasets, and evaluation protocols as a coupled empirical pipeline, and highlight open challenges, notably the persistent gap between predictive fidelity and downstream utility.

paper_title: Dynamic Network Transitions Preceding Auditory Hallucination Onset: A Systematic Review of Burst-Capture fMRI and EEG-fMRI Integration
paper_abstract: Auditory verbal hallucinations (AVH) are transient, internally generated percepts that emerge against spontaneous brain activity, yet most neuroimaging contrasts average hallucination ‘ON’ against ‘OFF’ periods and thereby dissolve the transition that is mechanistically decisive. This systematic review synthesises symptom-capture functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI), dynamic functional connectivity, electroencephalography (EEG) microstate, perfusion and simultaneous EEG-fMRI studies of AVH identified in five databases, and critically appraises seven transient-state estimators. We introduce ‘burst-capture’, an onset-anchored strategy in which brief hallucinatory episodes define the temporal frame and the pre-onset interval is the unit of inference. Onset-anchored studies consistently implicate superior temporal and primary auditory cortex, inferior frontal gyrus, hippocampus and thalamus. Dynamic analyses show that hallucination-relevant abnormalities are state-bound and invisible to static connectivity: hallucination proneness tracks reduced dwell time in states of default mode network (DMN)–task-positive anticorrelation; patients with AVH under-occupy, and switch less often into, a DMN–language antagonistic state; hallucination periods show more erratic switching and shortened EEG microstate class D; and stage-resolved effective connectivity implicates the salience network during emergence. Convergent perfusion, gamma-synchrony and prestimulus-state evidence supports a tonic vulnerability that lowers the threshold for a phasic network transition. We propose a transition-competition model in which AVH onset is a threshold crossing within a multistable network system, and specify the requirements of a valid burst-capture EEG-fMRI study: reaction-time-independent anchors, surrogate-data testing of state estimators and sign-aware EEG–BOLD fusion. Transition metrics, not averaged activation, should become the primary outcomes of hallucination neuroimaging.

paper_title: Autonomous Space Systems via Reinforcement Learning: Review, Challenges, and Future Directions
paper_abstract: Reinforcement learning (RL) is increasingly being investigated for spacecraft guidance, navigation, control, and mission autonomy, particularly where uncertainty, nonlinear dynamics, limited onboard computation, or changing operating conditions challenge conventional approaches. This review examines RL and closely related learning-based methods across major space-control applications, including attitude and orbit control, low-thrust and cislunar guidance, planetary landing, small-body operations, rendezvous and docking, space robotics, surface mobility, and mission-level autonomy. Reported results are assessed with respect to classical baselines, quantitative performance, robustness, computational cost, and validation fidelity from simulation to hardware and flight demonstrations. Across the literature, learned controllers often show advantages in adaptation, robustness to modeled uncertainty, and rapid onboard evaluation, while numerical optimization and classical control generally retain advantages in nominal optimality, interpretability, and established guarantees. Hybrid architectures, in which learning modifies or augments a conventional guidance or control law, provide some of the most consistent results. Important limitations remain in out-of-distribution generalization, benchmarking, statistical reporting, navigation realism, verification, implementation assurance, and independent high-fidelity validation. The review concludes with proposed benchmark problems, reporting practices, and a staged validation pathway for assessing learned controllers in increasingly realistic space-system environments.

paper_title: In Vivo Glutamatergic and GABAergic Biomarkers of Auditory Verbal Hallucinations in Schizophrenia: A Systematic Review and Synthesis of Meta-Analytic Evidence from Proton Magnetic Resonance Spectroscopy and PET Studies
paper_abstract: Auditory verbal hallucinations (AVH) are among the most distressing and treatment-refractory symptoms of schizophrenia. N-methyl-D-aspartate receptor hypofunction and parvalbumin interneuron deficits predict a regional excitation–inhibition imbalance in speech-processing cortex, but whether in vivo neurochemical imaging captures this imbalance in people who hallucinate is unclear. Following PRISMA 2020, we searched MEDLINE, Embase, PsycINFO, and Web of Science for proton magnetic resonance spectroscopy (1H-MRS) and positron emission tomography or single-photon emission computed tomography studies of glutamatergic or GABAergic markers in schizophrenia-spectrum disorders. Regional case–control estimates from published meta-analyses and mega-analyses were synthesized; AVH-stratified studies were synthesized narratively because voxel placement, metabolite composites, and hallucination metrics precluded valid pooling. Glutamatergic abnormalities were regionally patterned: thalamic glutamine (Hedges g = 0.53) and basal ganglia glutamate plus glutamine (Glx; g = 0.28–0.39) were elevated, medial frontal glutamate was reduced, and patient variability exceeded control variability. Pooled γ-aminobutyric acid (GABA) effects were nonsignificant (g = −0.004 to −0.30), and GABA-A receptor imaging showed no replicable differences. Across 5 AVH-stratified 1H-MRS cohorts, left superior temporal Glx or glutamate rose with hallucination severity, whereas medial prefrontal and anterior cingulate Glx fell (r = −0.30); GABA effects were null. In vivo evidence therefore favors a regionally dissociated temporo-cingulate glutamatergic gradient, rather than a global GABA deficit, as the neurochemical signature of AVH. Harmonized, medication-controlled, AVH-stratified multimodal studies are required before these measures can serve as clinical biomarkers.

paper_title: Do Patients Feel More Capable of Managing Their Own Health After Psychiatric Treatment? A Narrative Review of Patient Activation, Empowerment, Self-Management, and Recovery
paper_abstract: Psychiatric treatment is conventionally judged by symptom reduction and service use, yet recovery-oriented policy asks a different question: does treatment leave people more capable of managing their own health? This narrative review synthesises evidence on patient activation, empowerment, self-efficacy, illness self-management and personal recovery to determine whether, and under what conditions, people report greater capability after mental health care. Capability proved measurable, mutable and clinically meaningful: activation predicts self-management, medication adherence, quality of life and readmission, and is largely independent of sociodemographic characteristics. Self-management interventions in severe mental illness improve hope, empowerment, self-efficacy and self-rated recovery. Peer support yields small but consistent gains in empowerment and personal recovery (g = 0.15) without reliable effects on symptoms or service use; recovery colleges improve self-confidence and self-understanding but lack randomised evidence; and Illness Management and Recovery shows inconsistent effects that track participation. Shared decision-making, conversational feedback of patient-reported outcomes and facilitated psychiatric advance directives strengthen autonomy, the last roughly halving the likelihood of coercive crisis intervention. Internalised stigma, perceived coercion and clinician-dominated communication erode capability. The answer to the review question is a qualified yes: capability gains are reliable on person-centred outcomes when treatment deliberately targets them, but they are not an automatic by-product of symptom-focused care. Community mental health services should measure capability directly, train clinicians in collaborative communication and treat empowerment as an explicit clinical target.

paper_title: Digital Assessment, Optimisation and Prehabilitation for Older Adults Undergoing Major Surgery: A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: An increasing number of older adults are undergoing major surgery. Frailty, multimorbidity and sarcopenia, over and above chronological age, are major determinants of postoperative complications, loss of independence and mortality. Comprehensive geriatric assessment (CGA) and multimodal prehabilitation can mitigate this risk, but hospital-based pathways are constrained by workforce, transport and geography, and these barriers often exclude the frailest patients. This narrative review examines how digital technologies can support preoperative assessment, optimisation, and prehabilitation in older surgical patients. We outline the biological rationale for repeated, dynamic assessment of resilience; review electronic frailty indices, digital CGA, remote functional testing and wearable-derived measures; and appraise remotely delivered exercise, nutritional, psychological, cognitive and medical optimisation. Digital tools appear feasible and can stratify risk in older adults; however, there is not yet evidence that they improve clinical outcomes on their own, and the largest trial of home-based prehabilitation in frail older adults found no benefit, with low adherence. We describe two real-world models from the UK: a remotely delivered multidisciplinary service at University College London Hospitals (UCLH) and PreActiv, a rule-based, individualised digital platform. In 274 patients treated at UCLH, sit-to-stand performance and health-related quality of life improved after prehabilitation and remained above baseline after surgery. Finally, we discuss sensor validity, digital inclusion, governance, health economics and the potential role of artificial intelligence.

paper_title: Low-Cost, Open-Source and Wearable ECG Systems for Remote Cardiac Monitoring: A Review of Architectures, Signal Processing, Validation and Regulatory Pathways
paper_abstract: Cardiovascular diseases remain the leading cause of death worldwide, and most of this burden falls on low- and middle-income countries where access to electrocardiography (ECG) is limited. In the last decade, integrated biopotential front ends, open-source microcontroller platforms and ubiquitous smartphones have made it possible to build ECG monitors at a fraction of the cost of conventional equipment, while consumer wearables have shown that single-lead ECG can be recorded at population scale. This narrative review examines how low-cost, open-source and wearable ECG systems are designed and evaluated for remote cardiac monitoring. We describe the end-to-end architecture (electrodes, analog front ends, microcontrollers, wireless links, gateways and cloud back ends), the signal processing chain (denoising, signal quality assessment, QRS detection, delineation and heart rate variability), and the emerging role of artificial intelligence running on the cloud or directly on the device. We then discuss validation methodology, including reference databases, standardized metrics and agreement analysis, and summarize the regulatory, safety and data protection requirements that separate a research prototype from a medical device. An Arduino-based remote ECG system previously developed by the author is used as a reference case to illustrate common design choices and pitfalls. We conclude that technical feasibility is no longer the bottleneck; rigorous validation in target populations, signal quality management and regulatory-grade engineering now determine clinical impact.

paper_title: A Global Systematic Review of Health and Environmental Outcomes, Acceptability and Feasibility of Aquatic Foods in School Meals
paper_abstract: School meal programmes support children’s food security, health and learning. Aquatic foods, including fish, shellfish and seaweed, provide protein, essential fatty acids and micronutrients, and some have lower environmental impacts than terrestrial animal-source foods. However, evidence on their integration into school meals has not been systematically synthesised. We systematically reviewed peer-reviewed and grey literature in English and Spanish on aquatic foods in school meals. Searches of Web of Science, PubMed, Cochrane Reviews and FAO AGRIS, supplemented by manual searches, identified 1,052 records. Two reviewers independently screened 975 abstracts and 156 full texts. Risk of bias was assessed using tools selected according to study design, and findings were synthesised narratively across nutritional, health, cognitive, acceptability, operational, producer and environmental outcomes. Seventy-three publications from 29 countries met the inclusion criteria. Evidence was concentrated in high-income settings and focused primarily on fish. A small number of independent trials reported improvements in selected nutrient biomarkers and cognitive outcomes, although broader dietary interventions sometimes prevented attribution to aquatic foods alone. Acceptability varied with product form, preparation and familiarity; feasibility depended on cost, procurement, storage and supply chain capacity. Environmental outcomes varied by product, comparator and impact measure. Evidence on producer outcomes, and aquatic foods other than finfish remained limited, details on aquatic food source were rarely included in studies. Aquatic foods can contribute to nutritious and diverse school meals, but effective integration requires attention to nutritional objectives, acceptability, procurement, food safety and environmental performance. Research across diverse settings is needed to identify which aquatic foods, forms and implementation approaches deliver intended benefits. Future studies should assess consumption and nutritional outcomes alongside costs, environmental trade-offs and producer benefits, while reporting species and sourcing to support context-specific policy and programme design.

paper_title: Treatment Exit in Aging Multiple Sclerosis: A Critical Review of Discontinuation, De-Escalation, and Dose Reduction, with Implications for GCC Practice
paper_abstract: Background: Aging and prolonged disease stability prompt reassessment of multiple sclerosis disease-modifying therapy. Discontinuation, switching, dose reduction and interval extension are distinct strategies. Stability during treatment may reflect reduced inflammatory activity, continuing drug effects, or both; chronological age alone cannot establish that withdrawal will preserve control. Objective: To critically assess treatment-exit evidence, reconcile apparently conflicting findings, distinguish treatment effects from prognostic associations, and examine implications for Gulf Cooperation Council (GCC) practice. Approach: A targeted, web-assisted critical narrative review examined accessible primary studies, corrections, conference reports, trial registrations and regional documents through 1 November 2026. Comparisons considered population, mechanism, strategy, outcome, surveillance, residual exposure, restart and alignment of follow-up. No meta-analysis, independent duplicate screening or formal certainty grading was performed. Principal findings: In DISCOMS, new disease activity occurred in 12.2% of discontinuers versus 4.7% of continuers over two years: an absolute difference of 7.5 percentage points (95% confidence interval, 0.6–15.0); non-inferiority was not established. DOT-MS stopped early after significant inflammatory activity in 8/45 discontinuers versus 0/44 continuers. Differences in eligibility, MRI thresholds and follow-up prevent attribution of these findings to age alone. Selected older-adult cohorts report limited relapse activity, but disability and patient-reported outcomes remain less certain. Natalizumab and fingolimod cessation carry early reactivation concerns requiring explicit consideration of the subsequent treatment pathway. Anti-CD20 cessation studies show sustained suppression in some selected populations, although residual exposure, treatment selection and imprecision limit conclusions about durable treatment independence. The included evidence does not establish a reliable comparative reduction in serious infection following treatment exit. Lower-efficacy switching can increase recurrence, while findings for specified extended intervals cannot be generalized to arbitrary dose reductions. Kuwait supplies direct natalizumab interval-extension evidence in younger adults; other GCC cohorts mainly inform treatment context. Regional guidance offers practical criteria that require appraisal against primary evidence and local monitoring conditions. Conclusions: Treatment reassessment should compare specified alternatives with continuation, communicate relevant absolute outcomes and uncertainty, and distinguish estimated benefit–harm from regional applicability. An author-proposed framework organizes patient goals, reasons for change, inflammatory activity, disability trajectory, exposure, harms, observation and reassessment. Its accompanying minimum dataset supports prospective evaluation without assigning a risk score or universal stopping threshold. Neither the framework’s feasibility nor its clinical utility has been validated. Mechanism-specific comparative studies and coordinated GCC research should evaluate inflammatory recurrence, disability, serious infections, treatment burden and continuity of care. Such evaluation should distinguish elective reassessment from treatment interruptions caused by changing access arrangements.

paper_title: Do Patients Who Report High Satisfaction Actually Experience Meaningful Improvement in Functioning, Autonomy and Quality of Life? A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Background. Patient satisfaction is among the most widely collected and most consequential metrics in health care, embedded in reimbursement, public reporting and quality improvement, and frequently treated as a proxy for the care a patient received. Yet satisfaction is an expectation-anchored appraisal of an encounter, whereas functioning, autonomy and quality of life are states of the person. Whether the two move together determines whether satisfaction-weighted quality frameworks reward better outcomes or merely met expectations. Methods. We conducted a narrative review, searching MEDLINE, Embase, CINAHL and Web of Science to 31 August 2026 for evidence linking patient satisfaction or patient experience to functioning, autonomy or quality of life. We included psychometric and conceptual work on satisfaction measurement; observational and administrative studies relating experience to clinical quality, safety and utilisation; specialty evidence from elective arthroplasty, spine surgery, chronic pain and rehabilitation; trial and systematic review evidence on patient-reported outcome feedback, autonomy support and activation; and theoretical work on response shift and the disability paradox. Disconfirming evidence was sought explicitly. Results. The evidence is mixed and strongly context-dependent. Positive experience is often, though not consistently, associated with better clinical processes; a substantial countervailing literature reports null, domain-specific or inverse associations, including higher utilisation, expenditure and mortality, and satisfaction discriminates technical quality poorly. Divergence is clearest in elective surgery: satisfaction after total knee arthroplasty is 82–89% while 8–15% report frank dissatisfaction with function, up to 28% are dissatisfied despite high aggregate success, and fulfilment of expectations predicts satisfaction in 93% of arthroplasty studies whereas preoperative expectations predict it in only half. Satisfaction tracks present state rather than magnitude of change. In rehabilitation, 88% of patients who missed their functional goals were nonetheless satisfied, and functional gain ranked below family involvement, goal attainment, communication and pain control as a correlate of satisfaction. Autonomy support, patient activation and goal-anchored care relate more consistently to functional and quality-of-life outcomes than satisfaction does. Response shift, the anchoring of minimal important difference estimates to satisfaction, and the disability paradox further weaken the inference from satisfaction to improvement. Conclusion. High satisfaction is not a reliable surrogate for meaningful improvement in functioning, autonomy or quality of life. Satisfaction should be retained and repositioned as a distinct patient-evaluation outcome, reported alongside — never instead of — directly measured functioning, autonomy and quality of life. Frameworks dominated by satisfaction risk rewarding expectation-driven, low-value care while concealing the patients whose outcomes are worst.

paper_title: Growth-Index Parametrizations Beyond ΛCDM: A Review of Interacting Dark Energy, Modified Gravity, and Observational Tests
paper_abstract: The growth relation f = d ln D/d ln a ≃ Ωγm provides a compact description of linear structure formation whose interpretation depends on the background, perturbation equations, amplitude convention, and scale range. This critical review compares constant, redshift-dependent, density-based, and bounded-transition growth indices in general relativity (GR), interacting dark energy (IDE), and modified gravity (MG). A homogeneous energy-transfer rate does not determine IDE perturbations, while scale-dependent MG generally requires more than a redshift-only index. We distinguish density growth from the velocity response entering redshift-space distortions. A reproducible radiation-free flat-ΛCDM illustration gives m aximum f σ8 approximation errors of 1.123% for constant 6/11, 0.108% for an endpoint-matched Chevallier–Polarski–Linder (CPL)-like form, and 0.159% for an unoptimized bounded transition on 0 ≤ z ≤ 2. A separate phenomenological calculation illustrates scale dependence without asserting a viable MG theory. These examples provide neither observational constraints nor a physical IDE/MG model comparison. We identify weakly constrained transition limits and set out the perturbative and likelihood requirements for testing additional parametrization freedom and reassessing the reported high-growth-index indication.

paper_title: Advancing Inclusive Development: Institutional Barriers and Opportunities for the Economic Participation of Women, Youth and Persons with Disabilities: A Systematic Review
paper_abstract: Introduction: Institutional inclusion does not necessarily produce meaningful economic participation. Across the supplied literature, women, youth and persons with disabilities encounter policy implementation gaps, administrative burdens, discriminatory norms, financial exclusion, digital access constraints and weak transitions from education or training into work and enterprise. This review examined how institutional barriers and opportunities influence the economic participation of women, youth and persons with disabilities within inclusive development and socio-economic governance contexts.Methods: The researcher-selected databases and information sources were Google Scholar. The eligibility protocol restricted publication years to 2016–2026. The exact calendar date of search execution was not recorded in the verified identification provenance; this is distinct from the publication-year eligibility range. A systematic review searched Google Scholar for English-language peer-reviewed studies published from 2016 to 2026 using a predefined Boolean strategy.Results: Seven codes clustered into four categories and produced five analytical themes. Formal inclusion frequently failed during implementation; administrative design converted nominal access into practical exclusion; norms, discrimination and accessibility barriers patterned participation; finance and digitalisation operated as conditional opportunities; and capability-building was most promising when embedded in coordinated, locally responsive support systems. Evidence was broad on barriers but uneven on youth-specific lived experience, intersectionality, implementation fidelity and long-term livelihood outcomes. Bibliometric evidence mapped prominence and relationships but did not establish quality or causal strength.Discussion/Conclusion: Economic participation is shaped less by the existence of inclusive policies than by their enforcement, accessibility, institutional coordination and fit with local capabilities. Inclusive development therefore requires integrated governance, simplified procedures, accessible finance and technology, capability development and sustained multi-stakeholder support.

paper_title: A Systematic Review of the Integration of African Philosophies Such as Ubuntu as Research Philosophies in Academic Writing: Epistemic Confidence, Methodological Engagement, and Implementation Challenges
paper_abstract: Introduction: African philosophies, including Ubuntu, Botho, Sankofa and related epistemological traditions, are increasingly invoked in scholarship concerned with decolonisation, relationality, epistemic justice and contextually grounded knowledge. However, their use as explicit research philosophies or methodological paradigms remains conceptually uneven. This review examined how African philosophies are integrated and operationalised within academic writing, the epistemic confidence and methodological engagement reflected in the literature, the associated risks and barriers, and the contextual conditions.Methods: The researcher-selected databases and information sources were Google Scholar and ERIC. The eligibility protocol restricted publication years to 2016–2026. The exact calendar date of search execution was not recorded in the verified identification provenance; this is distinct from the publication-year eligibility range. A systematic review searched Google Scholar and ERIC using a verified Boolean strategy and applied eligibility limits covering English-language publications from 2016 to 2026.Results: The synthesis identified four analytical themes. African philosophies were presented as relational, situated and emancipatory bases for knowing; operationalisation was predominantly applied, plural and incremental rather than fully methodological; epistemic confidence was qualified by concerns about authenticity, adequacy and verification; and institutional structures continued to limit meaningful integration. Context, language, community relationships and intercultural dialogue shaped effective use. Evidence about researchers’ confidence was indirect and methodological accounts were less developed than conceptual claims.Discussion/Conclusion: The literature supports cautious confidence that African philosophies can inform research and scholarly practice, but it does not establish a single, mature or consistently operationalised African research methodology. Meaningful integration requires conceptual depth, linguistic and contextual engagement, institutional transformation and transparent methodological specification.

paper_title: Laser-Induced Optical Breakdown for Melasma and Photoaging: Molecular Mechanisms, Optical Biopsy Assessment, and Emerging Nanozyme-Based Adjuncts; A Systematic Review
paper_abstract: Background: Picosecond laser-induced optical breakdown (LIOB), particularly when generated using a diffractive lens array, creates spatially confined photomechanical microinjury with limited nonspecific thermal damage. This review evaluates the role of LIOB in melasma and photoaging, with emphasis on the distinction between pigment fragmentation and regenerative tissue re-sponses. Preclinical and translational studies indicate that LIOB may promote extracellular matrix remodeling through TGF-β/Smad signaling while attenuating matrix-degrading and inflamma-tory pathways, including MMP-9 and NF-κB. Cellular-resolution full-field optical coherence to-mography (CRFF-OCT), coupled with computer-aided image analysis, offers a non-invasive ap-proach for longitudinal assessment of melanin morphology, the dermal–epidermal junction, col-lagen architecture, and treatment-related structural change. Hyperbranched polymer dots (HPDs) are additionally considered as experimental nanozyme-based adjuncts because of their antioxidant and regenerative properties; however, their relevance to melasma remains preclinical. Collec-tively, LIOB, quantitative optical biopsy, and bioactive nanomaterials provide a conceptual preci-sion-medicine framework for treating melasma as a chronic photoaging-associated disorder, alt-hough further prospective validation is required before these components can be integrated into routine care. Objectives: To critically synthesize the available clinical and preclinical evidence on LIOB for melasma and photoaging, evaluate CRFF-OCT as a potential tool for structural assess-ment and treatment monitoring, and describe the current translational evidence for HPDs as ex-perimental adjuncts. Methods: A structured literature search was conducted using PubMed, Sco-pus, ScienceDirect, and Google Scholar, supplemented by manual screening of reference lists. The principal search period covered January 2015 to May 2026, with earlier landmark publications considered when relevant. Eligible publications addressed the clinical applications, biological mechanisms, imaging assessment, or potential adjunctive approaches related to picosecond LIOB, melasma, photoaging, and skin remodeling. Clinical, translational, and experimental evidence was considered. Findings were synthesized qualitatively because of the heterogeneity of the in-cluded evidence, and no meta-analysis was performed. The last search date for this study was February 23, 2026. Results: A total of 37 studies are included in this review, and they emcompass experimental studies, cohorts, and literature reviews. Available data suggests that LIOB may promote extracellular matrix remodeling through transforming growth factor-β (TGF-β)/Smad signaling while modulating matrix-degrading and inflammatory pathways, including matrix metalloproteinase-9 (MMP-9) and nuclear factor kappa B (NF-κB), which are key pathways to treating melasma and photoaging. Computer aided optical confluence tomography, combined with computer-aided image analysis, offers a noninvasive approach for longitudinal assessment of melanin morphology, the dermal–epidermal junction, collagen architecture, and treatment-related structural changes. Hyperbranched polymer dots (HPDs) demonstrate experimental antioxidant and regenerative properties, although their application as adjuncts in melasma remains at the preclinical stage. Limitations: The studies included in this review may demonstrate heterogeneity, as a formal risk-of-bias assessment was not conducted. Further prospective clinical studies may be required to establish the efficacy and safety of nanozyme-based approaches to treatment. Con-clusion: LIOB is a promising approach for addressing melasma and photoaging in terms of uti-lizing pigment fragmentation and triggering regenerative tissue responses in melasma. To moni-tor treatment results non-invasively, CRFF-OCT may provide valuable structural biomarkers as a reference. HPDs are an emerging adjunct to treatment monitoring as well. Protocol registration: The review protocol was not prospectively registered in a publicly accessible systematic review registry. Funding: No specific funding was provided for this systemati review.

paper_title: Income Gradients in Systolic Blood Pressure: Education Adjustment and Survey Using Weighted Regression in NHANES 2021-2023
paper_abstract: Income and education capture distinct but interrelated dimensions of socioeconomic resources. This study examines the association between the family income-to-poverty ratio (PIR) and measured systolic blood pressure (SBP), comparing estimates before and after adjustment for body mass index (BMI) and education. Four NHANES components were linked, and eligibility, repeated measurements, pregnancy status and variable completeness were assessed to obtain a common sample of 5019 adults. Three linear models incorporated examination weights, strata and primary sampling units, sequentially adjusting for demographic characteristics, BMI and education. Each one-unit higher PIR was associated with an SBP difference of -0.682 mmHg after demographic adjustment (95% CI -1.193 to -0.171), -0.656 after adding BMI (-1.193 to -0.119), and -0.201 after adding education (-1.014 to 0.612). Education adjustment substantially attenuated the income gradient, whereas BMI adjustment changed it little. Presenting these models together shows how the interpretation of income-related blood pressure differences depends on the dimensions of social resources included in the comparison.

paper_title: From Expectation to Experience: The Patient Expectation–Reality Gap in Psychiatric Consultations — A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Objective: To synthesize evidence on the gap between what patients expect from psychiatric consultations and what they experience, and on its origins, consequences and remedies.Methods: A narrative review, guided by the SANRA criteria, of conceptual frameworks, empirical studies, systematic reviews and meta-analyses from psychiatry, general medicine, psychotherapy and placebo research, identified through targeted searches of PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus and Google Scholar and by citation chaining.Results: Patients most consistently expect to be listened to, to receive emotional support and explanation, and to be told what the consultation will involve, whereas consultations are typically assessment-driven, shorter than anticipated and more often end in prescription or referral than patients expect. Stigma, delayed help-seeking, illness beliefs and time-pressured services amplify the gap, and the therapeutic alliance moderates it. Unmet expectations predict dissatisfaction and non-adherence; optimistic outcome expectations are associated with better outcomes (r = 0.18 across 12,722 patients); and expectancy mediates placebo and nocebo responses to antidepressants. Eliciting expectations, preparatory information, shared decision-making, communication-skills training and expectancy-sensitive framing of benefits and risks show promise, although trial evidence from psychiatric settings remains limited.Conclusion: The expectation–reality gap is a modifiable determinant of patient experience and outcome in psychiatry that warrants precise measurement and targeted intervention.Practice implications: Clinicians should routinely elicit patients' predicted and desired expectations, explain what the consultation involves, negotiate plans that visibly address patients' requests, and frame treatment benefits and side effects to minimize nocebo responses; services should protect time for psychosocial discussion and embed communication and shared decision-making training.

paper_title: Dynamic Network Transitions Preceding Auditory Hallucination Onset: An Integrative Review of Burst-Capture fMRI and EEG-fMRI Evidence
paper_abstract: Auditory verbal hallucinations (AVH) are discrete, self-limiting perceptual events, yet their neural basis has been characterised largely through static contrasts between hallucinating and non-hallucinating periods. Whether a reproducible sequence of large-scale network transitions precedes conscious hallucination onset remains unresolved. This integrative review, built on a structured search of five databases (1995–2025), synthesises burst-capture (symptom-capture) functional magnetic resonance imaging (fMRI) studies in which participants signalled episode onset and offset during scanning, together with time-resolved connectivity, electroencephalography (EEG) and simultaneous EEG-fMRI evidence. Capture studies converge on a fronto-temporal, insular and medial temporal signature of the hallucinatory episode. Ventromedial prefrontal and paracingulate activity begins several seconds before the onset report, with a mirror-image deflection before offset, and both precede the motor response. Hallucination-prone individuals spend less time in brain states with strong default mode/task-positive anticorrelation, and salience-network-centred switching is reduced, less persistent and more variable. EEG microstate class D shortens during hallucinations, auditory-cortical alpha synchrony rises around onset, and EEG-fMRI studies show that such electrophysiological markers can be mapped onto haemodynamic networks. We integrate these findings into a testable dynamic transition model: a vulnerable baseline gives way to a less differentiated cortical state, a salience-network switch, default mode withdrawal and fronto-temporal re-synchronisation that culminate in the percept, followed by a distinct offset signal. Because no study has yet ordered these events within one dataset, adequately powered single-trial EEG-fMRI capture designs with harmonised signalling are the decisive next step toward predictive and interventional markers.

paper_title: Anesthetic and Sedative Effects on Echocardiographic Parameters in Rat Models of Cardiomyopathy: A Critical Review
paper_abstract: Cardiomyopathies represent a heterogeneous group of diseases that lead to functional and structural impairment of the myocardium, frequently culminating in heart failure. Due to ethical and technical constraints inherent to human studies, rat models have become indispensable in experimental cardiology. Transthoracic echocardiography represents one of the most commonly used methods for assessing cardiac structure and function in experimental rat models of cardiomyopathy, due to its accessibility, non-invasiveness, ease of use, safety and cost-effectiveness. Almost all echocardiographic examinations in rats require a certain level of pharmacological sedation or general anesthesia to immobilize the animal and reduce motion-induced artifacts. A review of the literature reveals that only a few anesthetics are used in experimental practice. By far the two most prevalent choices are isoflurane and the ketamine-xylazine combination. Less frequently used are pentobarbital, the tiletamine-zolazepam combination, sevoflurane, and acepromazine. However, the interpretation of echocardiographic findings in experimental animals can be significantly biased by the effects of anesthesia primarily on the autonomic nervous system and cardiac contractility. Therefore the choice of anesthetic or sedative protocol represents an important, yet insufficiently standardized, methodological variable in the echocardiographic assessment of rat models of cardiomyopathy. Here we discuss the bias introduced by the use of sedatives/anesthetics when performing echocardiography in different rat models of experimental cardiomyopathy.

paper_title: GUI Grounding for Computer-Use Agents: A Survey
paper_abstract: Graphical user interface (GUI) agents automate tasks in digital environments by interpreting user goals and executing interface operations. GUI grounding serves as a critical link between high-level reasoning and low-level interaction execution in GUI agents. It maps users' operation intents to specific interaction targets and their spatial parameters, enabling agents to translate high-level decisions into executable interface actions. Advances in multimodal large language models (MLLMs) have substantially improved GUI agents' capabilities in autonomous operation. However, existing surveys primarily focus on complete GUI-agent systems, leaving grounding methods, data resources, and performance limitations insufficiently synthesized. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first comprehensive survey dedicated to GUI grounding. First, we establish a unified taxonomy along three complementary dimensions—learning paradigms, inference strategies, and target representations—to systematically characterize the core mechanisms and properties of existing methods. Second, we review training datasets, evaluation benchmarks, and metrics, tracing the evolution of data resources and evaluation tasks. Third, we conduct a comparative analysis of representative methods across evaluation benchmarks, identifying their strengths and limitations across target types, instruction complexity, and interaction requirements, while examining trade-offs between accuracy and inference cost. Our analysis reveals that GUI grounding research is expanding from explicit target localization in static interfaces toward implicit intent understanding, target resolution in dynamic interfaces, and spatial-parameter prediction for complex interactions. We discuss the resulting open challenges and future research directions.

paper_title: Health Financing, Health-System Strengthening, and Health Outcomes in Liberia and the Mano River Union: A Systematic Review
paper_abstract: Background: The Mano River Union (MRU) countries (Liberia, Sierra Leone, and Guinea) face persistent health-system constraints related to conflict, epidemics, underinvestment, and weak institutional capacity. Progress toward universal health coverage (UHC) requires evidence on how financing and system-strengthening strategies affect service access, equity, and resilience. This review synthesized evidence on health financing and health-system strengthening in Liberia and the wider MRU, including their implications for health outcomes, equity, and community health systems. Methods: This PRISMA 2020-compliant review was registered in PROSPERO (CRD420251243931). PubMed and African Journals Online were searched for English-language sources published from 1 January 2015 to 31 December 2025, and gray literature was sought from the World Health Organization, World Bank, UNICEF, African Development Bank, and Liberia Ministry of Health. Two reviewers independently screened records and extracted data, and primary empirical studies were appraised using the Mixed Methods Appraisal Tool 2018. Findings were integrated using narrative thematic synthesis within a health-systems framework informed by PECOS. Results: Database searches identified 1,254 records, and organizational sources identified six additional records. After 312 database duplicates were removed, 942 database records were screened; 934 were excluded, and eight reports were retrieved and assessed. All six organizational records were retrieved and assessed. No reports were excluded after full-text assessment, and all 14 reports were included, comprising six journal articles (including two reviews) and eight institutional or technical reports. Five themes emerged: chronic underfunding and low government prioritization of health; mixed, mechanism-dependent performance of financing reforms; geographic and socioeconomic disparities in maternal and child health access; central but donor-dependent community health systems; and Ebola-related disruption with uneven recovery. Governance fragmentation and donor coordination were cross-cutting concerns. Liberia's average health-budget allocation of 3.46% from 2010 to 2018 illustrates the financing gap. Conclusions: Although the evidence base is limited by heterogeneous designs, reliance on policy and technical sources, and the absence of Guinea-specific studies, evidence from the MRU indicates that underinvestment, inequity, and governance weaknesses continue to constrain health-system performance. More predictable domestic financing, equity-oriented reforms, and sustained support for integrated community health systems are priorities for advancing UHC in fragile and post-conflict settings.

paper_title: Fecal Incontinence in Patients with Irritable Bowel Syndrome: A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Fecal incontinence (FI) is the recurrent and uncontrolled passage of fecal material, in-cluding episodes of soiling or underwear staining. Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS) is a disorder of gut-brain interaction characterized by recurrent abdominal pain or dis-comfort associated with altered bowel habits, including diarrhea, constipation, or a mixed pattern. Although these conditions have traditionally been considered sepa-rately, increasing evidence suggests that they frequently overlap, especially in patients with diarrhea-predominant IBS. In this setting, FI should not be regarded as a simple consequence of anal sphincter weakness. Loose stools, urgency, altered colonic transit, rectal hypersensitivity, anorectal sensorimotor dysfunction, pelvic floor impairment, and reduced continence reserve may interact and promote leakage. Additional struc-tural, iatrogenic, and patient-related factors may further increase susceptibility. The overlap is often underrecognized because many patients do not spontaneously report fecal leakage, despite its relevant impact on quality of life and daily functioning. A careful history, direct but non-stigmatizing questioning, physical examination, symp-tom assessment, and selective investigations are therefore essential to identify the dominant clinical phenotype and exclude secondary causes. Treatment should be indi-vidualized and progressive, combining optimization of bowel habits and IBS-directed strategies with anorectal rehabilitation and, when needed, more advanced FI-directed treatments. Recognizing FI as part of the clinical spectrum of IBS may improve diag-nostic accuracy, promote earlier treatment, and support a more integrated and pa-tient-centered approach to care.

paper_title: The Political Economy of Municipal Governance: /Political Contestation, Coalition Stability and Local Economic Development in Post-2026 South Africa: A Systematic Review with Reference to eThekwini Metropolitan Municipality
paper_abstract: Introduction: Political contestation and coalition instability have become important features of South African municipal governance. The supplied evidence links unstable political arrangements with leadership turnover, delayed budgets, interrupted services and weakened long-term planning, while also indicating that coalition government is not uniformly harmful. Local economic development (LED) is additionally shaped by institutional capacity, policy coherence, stakeholder participation, resources and accountability. Methods: The researcher-selected databases and information sources were Google Scholar, ERIC. The eligibility protocol restricted publication years to 2017–2026. The exact calendar date of search execution was not recorded in the verified identification provenance; this is distinct from the publication-year eligibility range. A systematic review was conducted using Google Scholar and ERIC for English-language peer-reviewed studies published from 2017 to 2026. The recorded search strategy combined municipal governance, political contestation and LED concepts. Results: The synthesis found that coalition instability can redirect municipal attention from LED and service delivery toward political survival, but effects vary with coalition cohesion and institutional arrangements. LED performance was constrained by unclear mandates, weak skills, insufficient finance, limited coordination and inadequate monitoring. Political economy dynamics shaped whose interests were represented, with eThekwini-specific evidence indicating preferential treatment of formal businesses over street traders. Durable trajectories required political accommodation to be institutionalised through shared priorities, coherent planning, accountability and participation. Discussion/Conclusion: Political contestation influences LED through its interaction with administrative capacity, institutional rules and distributive power rather than through a simple coalition-versus-performance relationship. The evidence does not permit a firm prediction of eThekwini's post-2026 trajectory because direct evidence on its coalition dynamics and LED implementation remains limited.

paper_title: Human-AI collaboration and Explainability in Manufacturing Operations: A Systematic Literature Review
paper_abstract: Recent advances in artificial intelligence (AI) are accelerating digitalization in manufacturingoperations, yet many solutions remain difficult to scrutinize and operate in human-centeredways, which can hinder adoption. This study presents a systematic review to map primaryresearch on AI in manufacturing operations where human-AI collaboration is explicit orexplainable artificial intelligence (XAI) and human factors are addressed. Searches in Scopus andIEEE Xplore (2020 - 2026) identified 1.240 publications. After a rigorous screening, 177 studieswere included. All studies were coded through an operational lens combining decision domains(scheduling, maintenance, inspection-quality, process control, shop floor) with AI roles andevidence strength. The primary domains are maintenance and inspection-quality, where thedecision support is the most explored role. Furthermore, most of the studies lack a specific XAImodality, while lab and simulation environments are the most included studies. The reviewhighlights that a large share of AI research in operations is still maturing in its human-centeredoperationalization. We provide structured matrices to support evidence-based design andadoption of human-centered AI in manufacturing operations.

paper_title: Mapping the Frontier: An Analytical Review of Emerging Research Gaps in Public Relations Scholarship
paper_abstract: Public relations (PR) scholarship stands at an inflection point. The theoretical architecture that defined the field's maturation—Excellence Theory, the dialogic tradition, and relationship management—was constructed for an information environment that no longer exists. This analytical review synthesizes the most active research gaps in PR as they appear in the international literature through early 2026, organizing them into a coherent framework of four fault lines: technological disruption, sociopolitical role expansion, epistemological narrowing, and the persistent measurement–legitimacy problem. The review is positioned explicitly against the field's growing meta-literature of systematic reviews and bibliometric mappings, which it treats both as evidence and as an object of critique. Seven substantive gaps are examined: the automation of communication labor by generative artificial intelligence (AI); epistemological narrowing and the exclusion of the Global South; corporate social advocacy and PR's political turn; the unresolved evaluation and proof-of-value problem; practitioner precarity, gender, and wellbeing; PR's ambiguous position within the information-disorder ecosystem; and internal communication under hybrid work. For each gap, the review distinguishes descriptive deficits (understudied contexts) from theoretical deficits (inadequate constructs) and methodological deficits (design limitations). A dedicated discussion section interprets the cross-cutting pattern—namely, that the field's fragmented gaps are surface expressions of a single underlying renegotiation of foundational assumptions—and concise recommendations translate this diagnosis into an actionable agenda. The central contribution is a diagnostic map that reframes scattered critiques as a systemic transformation of the field's intellectual foundations.

paper_title: Primary Thyroid Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma: Clinical Features, Treatment Outcomes and Literature Review — A Brief Report
paper_abstract: Background: Primary thyroid lymphoma (PTL) is a rare extranodal malignancy accounting for 1%–5% of all thyroid neoplasms, with diffuse large B-cell lymphoma (DLBCL) being the most common and aggressive subtype. Due to its low incidence, clinical data remain limited. This study aims to describe the clinical features, diagnostic approaches, treatment and outcomes of primary thyroid DLBCL in a single-center case series. Methods: We retrospectively enrolled four consecutive patients with histopathologically verified primary thyroid DLBCL who received treatment at our institution between 2021 and 2026. All relevant clinical data were extracted from archived electronic medical records. No statistical comparative analyses were performed given the limited sample size. Results: The cohort comprised four females, with a mean age of 73.5 years (range, 50–88 years). All patients presented with a rapidly enlarging painless neck mass, and two (50%) exhibited compressive symptoms. Elevated thyroid autoantibodies (TPO-Ab and/or TG-Ab) were detected in three patients (75%), indicating underlying Hashimoto’s thyroiditis. Diagnostic procedures varied among individuals: fine-needle aspiration cytology (FNAC) and/or core-needle biopsy (CNB), partial thyroidectomy were applied for pathological confirmation. All cases were classified as DLBCL. One patient received R-CHOP immunochemotherapy, one received Pola-R-CHP, and two opted for observation management. Conclusion: This case series provides descriptive real-world observations of primary thyroid DLBCL among elderly Chinese with underlying Hashimoto’s thyroiditis. Findings from this small cohort cannot be generalized. Immunochemotherapy regimens including R-CHOP and Pola-R-CHP may be considered within individualized multidisciplinary strategies; further large-scale studies are required to validate therapeutic performance.

paper_title: Deciphering Viral Antigenic Relationships Through Antigenic Cartography: A Narrative Review
paper_abstract: Background: Antigenic cartography is a computational approach that quantitatively visualizes antigenic relationships among viral strains using serological data, including hemagglutination inhibition and virus-neutralization assays. Since its introduction in the early 2000s, it has substantially advanced the study of viral antigenic evolution by transforming complex serological measurements into interpretable antigenic maps, thereby facilitating assessment of antigenic diversity, immune escape, cross-reactivity, and vaccine–virus relationships. Objective: This review examines the historical development, methodological principles, applications, limitations, and emerging directions of antigenic cartography across clinically relevant viruses, with particular emphasis on its relevance to viral surveillance, antigenic drift monitoring and vaccine-strain selection. Methods: The literature was synthesized comparatively across major applications of antigenic cartography, encompassing human seasonal influenza and other viruses, including dengue, lyssaviruses, foot-and-mouth disease virus, Enterovirus A71, norovirus, rotavirus, SARS-CoV-2, and HIV. Particular attention was given to real-world applications, methodological advances, sources of uncertainty, and integration with genomic, structural, evolutionary, and computational approaches. Findings: Influenza remains the most extensively studied viral pathogen, where antigenic cartography has supported recognition of epidemiologically relevant antigenic transitions and informed vaccine decisions. Examples include the emergence of A/Fujian/411/2002-like H3N2 viruses during 2004–2005 and assessment of A/California/07/2009 during 2010–2011. Applications to other viruses demonstrate broader utility for characterizing antigenic landscapes and evaluating cross-protective immunity and vaccine performance. However, map reliability is influenced by serological assay variability, serum-panel composition, measurement noise, incomplete and geographically biased datasets. Limited inter-operability among serological, genomic, and structural datasets further restricts reproducibility and cross-study comparability. Future Directions and Conclusions: The field is transitioning from retrospective visualization toward predictive and mechanistically informed antigenic surveillance. Integration of artificial intelligence, protein language models, evolutionary modelling, structural vaccinology, and real-time genomic–serological surveillance could enable earlier prediction of antigenic drift, identification of emerging vaccine mismatches, and prioritization of candidate vaccine strains. Future platforms should incorporate standardized and automated serological measurements, inter-laboratory calibration, harmonized data standards, geographically representative datasets, experimental validation, and interpretable continuously updated models. Such integration could establish antigenic cartography as a scalable predictive framework for vaccine design and for strengthening preparedness against emerging viral threats.

paper_title: The Unequal Capture of South Africa’s Informal Economy: A Systematic Review of Indigenous and Immigrant Entrepreneurship
paper_abstract: Introduction: South Africa’s informal economy supports livelihoods, employment, food access and local exchange, yet market participation is shaped by unequal institutional, political and social conditions. The supplied literature documents immigrant-specific barriers involving permits, documentation, banking, policing and xenophobia, while also describing Indigenous and locally embedded entrepreneurship through community legitimacy, trust and relational value. However, direct comparative evidence on economic capture, profitability and formal-market access remains limited. Methods: The researcher-selected databases and information sources were Google Scholar, ERIC. The eligibility protocol restricted publication years to 2018–2026. The exact calendar date of search execution was not recorded in the verified identification provenance; this is distinct from the publication-year eligibility range. A systematic review searched Google Scholar and ERIC using a predefined Boolean strategy and an eligibility range of 2018–2026. Results: Immigrant status was associated with additional institutional and security barriers, including permit delays, restricted banking access, inadequate protection, xenophobic violence and exclusionary practices. Immigrant entrepreneurs nevertheless mobilised family, migrant, community and transnational networks as alternative resources. Indigenous and locally embedded enterprise was associated with community legitimacy, trust, livelihoods and relational value, but the evidence did not demonstrate universally greater Indigenous market capture. Shared constraints included finance, infrastructure, skills, technology, workspace and regulatory support. Inclusive governance and cooperation were proposed but not comparatively evaluated. Discussion/Conclusion: Status influences market access through layered institutional and social mechanisms, but it does not provide a sufficient standalone explanation of unequal capture. Immigrant-specific exclusion operates within broader informal-economy constraints, while network agency and local embeddedness can moderate disadvantage.

paper_title: Dexterous Robotic Hands in the Foundation-Model Era: A Full-Stack Survey of Hardware, Data, Cross-Embodiment Transfer, Learning, and Evaluation
paper_abstract: Dexterous robotic hands are increasingly coupled to large-scale human data and foundation models, yet progress in hardware, representation learning and evaluation is often assessed separately. This survey reviews work from January 2024 to early November 2026, with earlier studies included to establish technical lineages. We organize the literature into five interdependent layers: hardware; data collection and curation; cross-embodiment transfer; learning and foundation models; and evaluation and applications. Human hand-object understanding and tactile sensing provide two cross-cutting perspectives. A system-level architecture, comparative tables and five case analyses connect design choices across these layers. We distinguish within-study experimental comparisons from heterogeneous corpus statistics, vendor specifications and company-reported results. Three conclusions emerge. First, the value of human data depends on kinematic, visual and contact alignment, not recording volume alone. Second, shared action representations and foundation policies do not remove embodiment-specific constraints on force, latency and contact. Third, task completion is insufficient to establish physical correctness or deployment readiness. Evidence remains limited for zero-shot transfer of contact-rich skills between morphologically different hands, long-duration reliability, and cross-sensor tactile generalization. We identify eleven open problems and propose reporting interfaces and controlled comparisons that can make full-stack progress more measurable. The review is a structured narrative synthesis rather than a pooled performance ranking or an exhaustive systematic review.
comments: 45 pages, 8 figures, 21 tables. Structured narrative review of hardware, data, cross-embodiment transfer, foundation models, tactile sensing, and evaluation for dexterous robotic hands

paper_title: From Vision to Context: A Review of Prompt-Driven Target Volume Segmentation in Radiotherapy
paper_abstract: Accurate target volume (TV) segmentation is essential for radiotherapy (RT) planning but remains time-consuming. Moreover, the final contour depends on the expertise of the radiation oncologist. Although deep learning has improved medical image segmentation, image-only models cannot encode the clinical reasoning that governs TV delineation, particularly for the clinical target volume (CTV), where boundaries are defined by clinical knowledge rather than imaging features alone. Prompt-driven segmentation has recently emerged as a strategy to address this limitation. This work aims to review these approaches for RT TV segmentation with four objectives: (1) compare the different prompting techniques used; (2) compare their performance against image-only baselines; (3) assess how they are evaluated against standard metrics, including the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC), 95th Hausdorff distance, sensitivity, precision, and clinical assessment; and (4) identify the gaps needed for clinical translation. We systematically searched PubMed, Embase, and arXiv for studies incorporating geometric, clinical text, or interactive prompts into deep learning models for RT TV delineation. Thirteen studies met the inclusion criteria, spanning head and neck, breast, prostate, lung, cervix, and rectal cancers. Seven studies used clinical text prompting, four used geometric prompting, and two used interactive prompting; three combined modalities. Reported DSC ranged from 0.67 to 0.93, compared to 0.65 to 0.91 for image-only baselines. None reported sensitivity or precision. Clinical text prompting appears well suited to CTV delineation. Evidence remains limited, and standardized prompt engineering and clinical validation are needed before these approaches can be translated into routine RT practice.
comments: Submitted to Computerized Medical Imaging and Graphics

paper_title: A Survey of Nonlinear Filtering Methods for Data Assimilation and Recent Advances in Generative AI-Enabled Score Filters
paper_abstract: Many real-world applications, such as numerical weather prediction or wildfire tracking, involve modeling highly nonlinear dynamical systems that are chaotic and influenced by various sources of uncertainty. To improve model prediction accuracy and reduce such uncertainties, data assimilation (DA) combines the dynamical model with partial, noisy observations to estimate the evolution of the system's state. Doing so depends on solving the optimal filtering problem: computing the conditional distribution of a hidden state given a sequence of observations. Classical approaches fail along three distinct axes: Kalman-based methods assume Gaussian posteriors and produce biased estimates under nonlinear observation operators; particle-based methods represent distributions with weighted samples and collapse in high dimensions due to the curse of dimensionality; and kernel-based methods move beyond discrete particle representations but cannot maintain their density approximation affordably as dimension grows. The Ensemble Score Filter (EnSF) avoids all three constraints by encoding the filtering density in a score function and approximating that score with a training-free Monte Carlo estimator, enabling stable filtering in high-dimensional, chaotic systems. This survey traces EnSF's mathematical foundations, establishes it as the state of the art for non-Gaussian, high-dimensional filtering, and examines fourteen extensions that expand its operational reach. Twelve of the fourteen extensions preserve this training-free Monte Carlo estimator at the core of the update, with only two departing from it to achieve planetary-scale deployment.

paper_title: Machine Learning for Live-Birth Prediction After IVF/ICSI From Structured Clinical Data: A Systematic Review, Meta-Analysis, and Critical Appraisal
paper_abstract: Machine-learning models predicting live birth after in vitro fertilisation (IVF) or intracytoplasmic sperm injection (ICSI) from routine clinical data report performance from near chance to near perfect. We systematically reviewed these models under PRISMA 2020, searching OpenAlex, Scopus and Web of Science to 22 October 2026, appraised them with PROBAST+AI and TRIPOD+AI, and pooled their discrimination with random-effects meta-analysis on the logit scale. We define what fixes the meaning of a model's output (decision point, endpoint, unit of analysis, data source) and map the 48 included studies by model family, decision point and validation design. Models evaluated only internally pooled to an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.814, against 0.756 (95% prediction interval 0.546-0.889) for models evaluated on a later period or another centre, and 0.764 for studies not at high risk of bias; neither difference was significant, and heterogeneity was extreme. Models whose decision point was not stated pooled to 0.910, the only significant moderator in meta-regression. Against logistic regression fitted to the same data, the best machine-learning model gained a pooled 0.056 AUC (95% CI 0.017-0.090). Of 48 studies, 47 were at high or unclear risk of bias, only four assessed the calibration slope, and no model has evidence of clinical impact. The certainty of the pooled evidence is low to very low; the gains that survive validation came from staging predictions to decision points and local calibration, not deeper architectures.
